answers.studentAnswer: A stack is a linear data structure that operates under the LIFO (Last In First Out) principle. This means elements are pushed onto the top and popped off the top. A great example of a stack is the back button on a browser which pops the previous webpage off the navigation stack, or a pile of plates. On the other hand, a queue uses the FIFO (First In First Out) rule, where items enqueue at the back and dequeue from the front. Examples are printer queues and ticket counters.

answers.studentAnswer: Binary Search Trees (BSTs) are binary trees where nodes on the left subtree are smaller than the parent node and nodes on the right subtree are larger. When we search, insert or delete nodes in a BST, it takes average time of O(log n) because we can discard half the tree at each step. But if the BST becomes skewed (like a straight line of nodes), it degrades to worst-case complexity of O(n) because we have to traverse all elements sequentially.
